messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are cracking—even the soldiers at the checkpoints know it. The banks are tightening their grip, the censuses are canceled, and the kids in the streets are singing what their parents whisper. Something’s coming, and soon. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we don’t know if the roof will fall or if someone’s still holding the beams from above."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—like the tide’s turning, but slowly, without anyone shouting about it. The old guard’s still standing, but their shoes are untied, and the kids at the wedding didn’t even notice the music stopped for a second. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to trip over our own feet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—less like tension before a storm, more like the quiet before a shift. The usual cracks are still there, but the regime’s grip seems looser in ways that don’t add up to panic yet. Keep your ears open, but don’t let your guard down—this could be the calm before something, not just another false alarm."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—like the ground shifting underfoot, but no one’s admitting they feel it too. The kids are talking louder, the old guard is whispering, and the money’s still coming… for now. Something’s coming, but whether it’s a storm or just the calm before the usual crackdown, I don’t know yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’ll know soon enough."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are cracking—even the ones we couldn’t see. People aren’t just talking anymore; they’re moving things, fixing roofs, and making quiet plans. The question isn’t *if*, but *when*, and whether we’ll be ready."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different now—not just tension, but something shifting under the surface. The usual cracks are widening, and the people who’ve always known how to read the signs are quietly packing their bags. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t a storm, it’s the calm before one."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are cracking—small, but you can feel the draft. The old men are still standing together in public, but the soldiers are restless, the money’s drying up, and the doctors are whispering in the back rooms. Something’s coming, but no one knows yet if it’ll be a storm or just rain. Stay sharp—this month, even the shadows have eyes."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first cracks. The usual signs are all there, but the real question is whether the roof comes down fast or piece by piece. Stay sharp, and keep your plans quiet—this isn’t the time for loud moves."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, and no one’s pretending it isn’t. The usual signs are all there, but the question isn’t *if* something’s coming, it’s how fast. Stay sharp, but keep it quiet—we don’t know who’s still watching, or what they’ll do when the cracks show."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but you can feel it. The banks are tightening, the orders are getting sloppy, and even the neighbors are talking like it’s 1989 again. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are cracking—more than we’ve seen before. The old rules don’t apply anymore, and even the ones who used to enforce them are looking the other way. Let’s stay sharp, but quietly. The time for waiting might be running out."*"
Sender 12: "*"The cracks are showing—even the elite can’t agree on basic orders, and the soldiers at the old base are fresh faces, not the usual ones. People are talking louder, spending more, and acting like they’re staying put for the long haul. But don’t let the quiet borders fool you—when the regime starts polishing its lies, it’s because the truth is getting harder to hide. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. We’ll know soon enough if they’re just stumbling or about to fall."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s rushing to push them down yet—people are too busy just trying to get by. The real question is whether the regime’s foreign friends will throw it a lifeline before the whole thing comes down on its own."*"
Sender 14: "*"Things are shifting, but not fast enough to feel safe—yet. The cracks are there, but the regime’s still holding on by managing the fractures, not fixing them. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let hope or fear rush you into anything. We’ll know more when the grumbling turns to action—or when the banks finally say no."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are cracking—just enough to let the light in, but not enough to bring them down yet. People are testing the air, and the regime’s grip feels looser than it did last month, but don’t mistake hesitation for weakness. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch the small things—they’re the ones that matter now."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the whole house or just the paint. The usual noise is gone—even the loudest voices are whispering now. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The air feels different, but the wind could shift fast."*"
Sender 17: "*"The regime’s still holding, but it’s like watching someone run on fumes—they’re moving, but you can hear the engine straining. The streets are quiet, but not in the way they used to be; more like the calm before something shifts. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves—we’re not the only ones watching."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but they’re adding up. The air feels different, like something’s shifting, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just the wind changing. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’ll know soon enough which way it’s going to break."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure yet if it’s an earthquake or just the first tremors. The usual whispers in the backrooms have gone quiet, and even the watch groups are talking less about theft and more about what comes next. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could still go either way."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the foundation giving way or just the paint peeling—either way, the air feels different. Keep your heads down, but don’t be surprised if the usual rules start bending soon. And if you’ve got a stash of basics, now’s the time to make sure it’s quiet and secure."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different now—like the ice is cracking underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s the whole lake or just a thin spot. The clinic’s stocking up, the embassies are locking their doors, and even the song on every radio is singing what we’ve all been thinking. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake hesitation for strength—this might be the moment we’ve been waiting for, or the calm before something worse. Either way, we should be ready."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels different now—like the walls are cracking, but the paint’s still wet. The song’s playing louder, the censors are blinking, and even the generals are whispering. But don’t mistake the noise for the storm yet—someone’s still paying the bills, and the courts are humming along like nothing’s wrong. Stay sharp, but keep your head down. The wind’s shifting, but we don’t know which way it’ll blow."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are still standing, but the foundation’s shifting—you can feel it in the way people move now, like they’re testing the ground before each step. The elites are holding hands in public, the banks are whispering, and the hospitals are running out of bandages before the fight’s even started. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake the quiet for safety—this isn’t over, it’s just choosing its moment."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the whole thing coming down or just the paint peeling. The fixers are gone, the contracts are signed, and even the courts are moving on their own—so either we’re all being lulled into a false calm, or the machine’s running on fumes. Either way, people are packing their bags, not just sharpening their pens."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are cracking—even the generals are whispering, and the bankers aren’t running. But the real question isn’t if, it’s when, and whether the army will step in to hold things together or let it all come down. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to be the first to blink."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
